review_notes: Reviewed all 192 lines, relevant normalization and cutoff lemmas, and downstream uses. The proposed generalization is source-supported but has not been checked by running Lean.

findings.excerpt: (hmass : ∀ a, |selectedResidueDensityMass q T V (D a) - 1| ≤ ηnorm)
findings.problem: The normalization assumption controls every base separately, although the joint law has just one normalization denominator: selectedJointDensityMass. Consequently, these theorems exclude densities whose individual masses vary substantially but whose average is close to one.
findings.proposed_change: In both theorems, replace this binder by `(hmass : |selectedJointDensityMass bases q T V D - 1| ≤ ηnorm)`, leaving the other assumptions and conclusion unchanged. Add a global-mass variant of the weighted-reference comparison and spatial-cutoff helper: retain their existing raw-test and indicator arguments, but bound `normalizedDensityTest_remove_normalization` directly with the new hmass instead of applying selectedJointDensityMass_close. The complex-to-real conversion remains unchanged. The existing caller can obtain the new assumption using selectedJointDensityMass_close. Retain hD and hbases: positive joint mass is still required, empty bases remain excluded, and individual density masses may now be zero.
findings.benefit: Users can obtain a useful probability bound from accurate joint normalization without proving unnecessarily strong uniform normalization at every base. The proof uses the existing normalization estimate and requires no new mathematical estimate.
